claims.text: The test system is a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy thin coating on a conventional metal substrate.
The as-deposited coating has a uniform grain-size distribution.
The as-deposited coating has a metastable phase balance.
A tailored post-deposition annealing treatment will refine the coating grains relative to the as-deposited condition.
Reducing grain size increases grain-boundary density.
Increased grain-boundary density promotes dynamic recrystallization during high-temperature sliding.
Increased grain-boundary density enhances grain-boundary sliding.
Dynamic recrystallization and grain-boundary sliding distribute plastic deformation more uniformly.
More distributed plastic deformation reduces localized stress concentrations.
Grain refinement shifts the dominant deformation mode away from solely dislocation-mediated plasticity toward grain-boundary-mediated deformation.
The annealed, grain-refined coating will have a lower wear rate than the as-deposited coating.
The annealed, grain-refined coating will exhibit less microscopic deformation damage, including reduced wear-track depth.
The annealed coating will show microscopic evidence of increased grain-boundary sliding relative to the as-deposited coating.
The predicted wear and deformation changes should hold during sliding at 600–800 °C under controlled loading and environmental conditions.
The magnitude of wear reduction and the deformation-mode transition may vary with annealing parameters and coating thickness.
A lack of statistically significant wear-rate reduction or a lack of transition toward grain-boundary-mediated deformation under matched test conditions would falsify the proposed mechanistic link.
